newsitem.title: UK: Early Italy budget approval 'very useful' - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Early Italy budget approval 'very useful' - Prodi.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday that early parliamentary approval of Italy's 1998 budget would be "very useful".
"This is a date in the political diary in Italy. It would be very useful to anticipate (it)," Prodi told reporters after talks with British Prime Minister John Major.

Prodi wants Italy to be among the founder members of the European economic and monetary union (EMU) and has proposed moving the deadline for parliamentary approval of next year's budget forward by four months to mid-August to boost confidence in Italy's financial credentials.
Prodi said the budget timetable would have to be discussed with Italian opposition in the coming few days.
